children: , the consumer-technology powerhouse, entered its September 9 product event under fresh pressure from two aggressive premium rivals. Huawei priced its Mate XT2 at $2,980, while Xiaomi unveiled the $1,540 18 Fold. With U.S. markets closed Monday, Apple shares remained at Friday's $319.97 close after tumbling 2.5%.

China is becoming a harder battlefield. Huawei captured 22.6% of the country's smartphone market in the second quarter, beating Apple's 18.1%, and dominated foldables with a 68% shipment share. Apple still brings enormous firepower: fiscal third-quarter revenue surged 16% to a record $109.4 billion, powered by $54.25 billion in iPhone sales.

That dependence cuts both ways. The iPhone delivered roughly 49.6% of quarterly revenue, so losing premium buyers would hit Apple's financial engine directly. At $319.97, the stock trades 12.35% above its GF Value estimate of $284.79, signaling that investors have already priced in plenty of confidence. Apple does not need to chase every foldable gimmickbut its next product cycle must keep high-end customers loyal without cracking the 50.1% companywide gross margin supporting that premium valuation.

title: Apple's $320 Stock Faces Huawei's 68% Foldable Fortress
